newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian stocks quiet, some dealers see falls.
newsitem.headline: Estonian stocks quiet, some dealers see falls.

text.p: Estonian shares firmed slightly on Friday amid sluggish trade and some traders forecast a weaker market next week.
"The market was quiet and it is expected to remain so, however next week's market should go lower as people are wanting to sell," one dealer said.

The Tallinn stock exchange index rose 0.86 percent to close at 186.85 on turnover of 28.4 million kroons on the official list. After a rally at the start of the year, shares recently had a downward correction and have drifted for the last few sessions.
Savings Bank stocks were buoyed by news that it was seeking a partner bank in Lithuania, which may involve the purchase of a stake or a whole bank, dealers said.
Savings Bank was the most traded stock with volume of 9.1 million kroons to finish up 0.60 kroons at 86.35 kroons.
"News of Saving bank beginning negotiations for a Lithuanian partner was excellent for their stocks," said a trader.
Hansapank turned over 7.2 million kroons to gain 0.30 kroons for a close of 177.75 kroons.
In other stocks, Union Bank's volume was 4.3 million kroons to firm by 0.25 kroons to 40.50. Tallinna Pank gained 0.18 kroons to end at 66.00 kroons after trade of 3.4 million kroons.
On the over-the-counter market trade was sluggish with a volume of 4.9 million kroons.
Rakvere meat plant slipped 0.80 kroons to close at 15.65 with a turn over of 3.2 million kroons.
Norma also dipped 0.05 kroons to close at 15.65 kroons with small turnover of 0.637 million kroons.
